result_semantic_payload.summary: The device owner's chat account (file:/chat/account_main.log) self-describes as the main operator (总操盘) of the scheme, stating that all money passes through their hands and they handle account settlement while others only recruit. However, the README (file:/README.txt) explicitly notes that such a self-descriptive boast is not independent proof of the role, and no corroborating identity or operational data links the owner to the ledger flows (file:/ledger/flows.txt). Therefore, the owner's actual role can only be asserted at the strength of an uncorroborated self-assertion; it cannot be confirmed as fact given the available corroboration.

claim_candidates.text: The device owner's chat account claims to be the main operator (总操盘) of the scheme, with all money passing through their hands and they handle account settlement while others only recruit.

The README states that the chat log is the device owner's own account, but a self-descriptive boast is not independent proof of the role, and no corroborating identity or operational data links the owner to the ledger flows.

limitations: No corroborating identity or operational data links the owner to the ledger flows.
The chat log is a self-assertion and does not constitute independent proof of the role.
warnings: A self-descriptive boast in a chat is a statement that the statement was made; it is not independent proof of the role.
